default 0 · -180 to 180

Degrees the bend's direction turns each step. With Pitch / Step, a helix

Gravitropic Setpoint
Surface
Flarenumbermappable
default 0.5 · 0 to 2 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for the stems level

How much the base of each stem widens into the ground, as a fraction of its radius. A stronger flare also runs higher up the stem

Lobeswhole numbermappable
default 5 · 0 to 8 on the slider (0 to 16 typed) · shown for the stems level

Buttress lobes around the flare, like the roots swelling out of a trunk's base. 0 keeps the flare round

Gnarlnumbermappable
default 0.3 · 0 to 1 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for the stems level

How much the stems wander and kink between nodes instead of running straight, at a scale of a few trunk widths. Leaves and flowers move with them

Barknumbermappable
default 0.3 · 0 to 1 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for the stems level

Surface unevenness of the stems: broad lumps sized to each stem's own thickness. Fine bark grain belongs in the bark texture

Twistnumbermappable
default 0.1 · -1 to 1 on the slider (-2 to 2 typed) · shown for the stems level

How far the stem turns about its own axis as it grows, in turns per 20 radii of length. Spirals the bark texture, ribbed or winged sections and the flare lobes. Negative turns the other way

Masks
Listlist

A branching level's masks: attribute, invert, a preview eye (where this mask kept / removed the level's branches), mute. data is the active level.

Attributechoice
default Height · shown for branch levels
Height

How far up the plant the organ sits (0 base, 1 top)

Branch Depth

How many levels of branching from the main stem -- 0 on the main stem, rising with each branch order (normalised to the plant's deepest branch)

Branch Index

A distinct value per branch, so you can pick out particular branches (normalised across the plant's branches)

On Branch

0 on the main stem, 1 on any branch -- the simple stem-vs-branch split

Node Index

Which node up its own axis the organ sits at, 0 at the base to 1 at the tip

Factor

Position along the organ's own axis, 0 at the axis base to 1 at its tip

Age

When the organ was made, 0 with the plant's first growth to 1 at the last -- low is old, high is new

Split Depth

How deep inside a fork / inflorescence the organ sits, 0 on vegetative stem rising with each split

Shade

How shaded the organ is by the plant's own canopy, 0 in open sky to 1 fully shaded -- sampled from the self-shading light field, so a dense clump reads its shaded interior

Bloom

A flower's place on the bloom order (flowers only)

Random

Seeded per-organ noise, for scattered thinning

Apex

1 on a shoot's own tip bud (its apex), 0 on axillary buds and every other organ -- keep only tip buds, or invert to keep only side buds

Custom Attribute

One of this plant's own attributes (Mapping & Classification panel): a distance to an object, noise, or two channels combined

Class

One of this plant's named classes (Mapping & Classification panel): 1 where that class's own mask stack keeps the point, 0 elsewhere -- build a class once, reuse and chain it

On Inflorescence

1 on an inflorescence -- the flowering nodes past an axis's leafy part, and the branches and stalks the inflorescence releases -- 0 on the leafy stem. Invert to keep only the vegetative part

Minnumber
default 0 · 0 to 1 · shown for branch levels

Low edge of the keep band. Points below Min are dropped

Maxnumber
default 1 · 0 to 1 · shown for branch levels

High edge of the keep band. Points above Max are dropped -- so Min 0.4, Max 0.5 keeps only the 0.4-0.5 slice

default On organs · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Where this component's instances go -- several at once: on grown organs, at nodes/terminals/junctions, along the stems, and/or scattered at random

On organs

Nodes

Internodes

Terminal

Intersections

Random

Basal

Basal Countwhole numbermappable
default 8 · 1 to 40 on the slider (1 to ∞ typed) · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Basal placement: how many leaves in the rosette at the base of each stem (each turning by the Phyllotaxis spiral; a whorl puts that many at each)

Sizenumbermappable
default 1 · 0 to 4 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

Scales this component's instances on top of the organ's own size. On a Flower it is the flower size; on a Bract (On Organs) it is the bract's size as a fraction of the foliage leaf its flowering node would have carried - full-sized on dead-nettle, scale-like on salvia - so bracts follow the Leaf Size curve up the stem. On the first Fruit component (On Organs) it is the fruit size, and fruit weigh with its cube. On a Bud it is the bud size

default Alternate (spiral) · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Alternate (spiral)

One instance per node on a golden spiral (137.5 deg)

Distichous

One per node, alternating 180 deg -- two ranks

Opposite

A pair at each node, aligned up the stem

Decussate

A pair at each node, each rotated 90 deg from the last

Whorled

Three per node, evenly spaced

Phyllotaxis Spiralnumbermappable
default 137.5078° · 0° to 360° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Divergence angle -- how far each successive generated point turns around the stem from the last. 137.5 deg is the natural golden-spiral default

Whorlwhole numbermappable
default 1 · 1 to 8 on the slider (1 to ∞ typed) · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

How many instances sit together at each position, spaced around the stem (a whorl). 1 is a single spiral

Whorl Spacingnumbermappable
default 0° · 0° to 360° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Pitchnumbermappable
default 0° · -5156.6202° to 5156.6202° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Foldnumbermappable
default 0° · -179.9998° to 179.9998° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Roll Selfnumbermappable
default 0° · -179.9998° to 179.9998° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Parent Rollnumbermappable
default 0° · -179.9998° to 179.9998° · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Weightnumbermappable
default 0.0001 · 0 to 0.002 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for Leaf

How heavy one full-size leaf of this component is, on the same relative scale as Flower Weight. It loads the stems for the grown leaves this component owns (the first leaf component placed On Organs); leaves placed at nodes, internodes or the base are drawn after the bend and weigh nothing

Skynumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1 · shown for Leaf, Bract

Fruit
Fruit Setnumbermappable
default 1 · 0 to 1 · shown for Fruit

Fraction of flowers that set fruit, rolled per flower. The rest are unpollinated and drop at fruit-set. 1 means every flower fruits

Weightnumbermappable
default 0.0015 · 0 to 0.02 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for Fruit

How heavy a full-size ripe fruit is, on the same relative scale as Flower Weight - heavier, which is what bows a fruiting branch. Like the flower, mass grows with the CUBE of Fruit Size. Fruit exists only inside the calendar fruit window, so a branch droops as its fruit ripens and springs back after fruit-drop

Inflorescence
Typechoice
default Solitary · shown for Flower

How the flowers are arranged where a stem finishes

A control listed as inert on a kind does nothing there. A kind with no pedicels ignores the pedicel controls; a terminal cluster ignores the flowering-gradient curves; only flat-topped kinds use the head controls; only relayed kinds use relay rotation. Why it works this way: Inflorescence types.

NoneNONE
none · pedicels

No flowers at all. Stems finish their development and stop, the same plant as any other kind minus its inflorescence - for foliage species, and for the branch a catkin hangs from, which has to be able to mature without turning into an inflorescence itself. Different from an indeterminate plant with nothing to flower with: those stems never stop, and grow on until the plant runs out of developmental span

SolitarySOLITARY
terminal flower · sessile

One flower at the tip of each stem

RacemeRACEME
flowering region · pedicels

Flowers on short pedicels along a continuing tip (foxglove, delphinium)

SpikeSPIKE
flowering region · sessile

Like a raceme but the flowers sit directly on the stem, no pedicels (plantain, many grasses)

CorymbCORYMB
flowering region · pedicels · flat-topped

A raceme whose lower pedicels are longer, bringing every flower up to about one level (yarrow)

UmbelUMBEL
apex cluster · pedicels · terminal cluster · no flowering gradients

Every pedicel radiating from one point at the tip, filling a dome right through its centre (allium)

Flat UmbelFLAT_UMBEL
apex cluster · pedicels · terminal cluster · flat-topped · no flowering gradients

An umbel whose pedicels are solved to land on one plane, so the head reads flat (cow parsley, Orlaya)

CatkinCATKIN
flowering region · pedicels

The stems bear no flowers themselves and hang catkins at their nodes instead - hazel, birch, willow. The one type here that is not something a stem turns into at its tip: a hazel's twigs go on being twigs and carry catkins along their length, on short stalks. Shape them in the Catkins box below. They are modelled rather than instanced, so they hang under their own weight and need no asset assigned

PaniclePANICLE
branched · pedicels

A branched raceme: the stem carries branches rather than flowers and does not flower itself, and each branch repeats that until the last one, which flowers (oat, astilbe, yucca). Its depth is Branching Depth below, counted inside the inflorescence and independent of Max Branch Order - so a tree can carry panicles on twigs that are already several branch orders deep

VerticillasterVERTICILLASTER
flowering region · pedicels

Rings of flowers spaced up the stem, each subtended by a pair of leafy bracts, with bare stem between them - the false whorl of the mint family (dead-nettle, motherwort, mint, salvia). Sets Flowers per Whorl and Bract Size, which are ordinary controls the other flowering kinds can use too. Botanically each ring is two condensed cymes rather than a true whorl; this builds a real ring, which reads the same at mint density

Cyme (custom)CYME
relay · sessile · relayed

The tip flowers first and stops, and growth carries on from shoots just below it, each repeating the pattern. This is the unstamped form: set Relays per Node and Relay Rotation yourself. The four named cymes below - Scorpioid, Helicoid, Dichasium, Pleiochasium - are this same mechanism with those two numbers already set, and are what you want unless you are after a combination they do not name

Scorpioid CymeSCORPIOID
relay · sessile · relayed

A zigzag chain: the tip flowers and one shoot below it carries on, alternating sides each time, so the whole spray kinks from side to side in one plane (forget-me-not, comfrey, heliotrope). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 180. How hard it zigzags is Branch Angle in the Branching box - +90 grows straight on with no kink, lower values fork harder every relay

Helicoid CymeHELICOID
relay · sessile · relayed

Like a scorpioid cyme but every relay arises on the same side rather than alternating, so instead of zigzagging the spray coils (Alstroemeria, sundew, many nightshades). Sets Relays per Node to 1 and Relay Rotation to 0 - that single number is the whole difference between this and a scorpioid cyme

DichasiumDICHASIUM
relay · sessile · relayed

The familiar forked cyme: the spent tip is flanked by two shoots, each of which forks again, doubling every generation (chickweed, campion, most pinks). Sets Relays per Node to 2 and Relay Rotation to 90, so successive forks cross rather than stacking in one plane. Note the count doubles per Branching Depth

PleiochasiumPLEIOCHASIUM
relay · sessile · relayed

Three or more shoots in a whorl below each spent tip, giving a broad umbel-like spray (spurge). Sets Relays per Node to 3 and Relay Rotation to 60. The count multiplies by Relays per Node every Branching Depth, so it grows very fast - three at depth 3 is 27 flowers

Compound SpikeCOMPOUND_SPIKE
compound · flowering region · sessile

A spike of spikes: every node of the flowering stem carries a whole spike of its own instead of one flower. Sets Type to Spike and Branching Depth to 1 - the dropdown then reads Spike, because that is what this is

Compound CorymbCOMPOUND_CORYMB
compound · flowering region · pedicels · flat-topped

A corymb whose flowers are themselves corymbs, so the head reads as a broad flat spray of little flat sprays (elder, yarrow). Sets Type to Corymb, Branching Depth to 1, and the Branching box - branches short, well spaced, finely tapered and arched

Compound UmbelCOMPOUND_UMBEL
compound · apex cluster · pedicels · terminal cluster · no flowering gradients

An umbel of umbels: each ray of the head ends in a whole umbel of its own. Sets Type to Umbel, Branching Depth to 1 and a long branch length, so the umbellets stand clear of one another

Compound Flat UmbelCOMPOUND_FLAT_UMBEL
compound · apex cluster · pedicels · terminal cluster · flat-topped · no flowering gradients

The cow parsley and hogweed form: rays from one point, each ending in its own flat-topped umbel. Sets Type to Flat Umbel, Branching Depth to 1, and the Branching box - ten long, slender, gently arched rays

Attachment Locationchoices
default Terminal · shown for Flower

Where the inflorescences arise - at the tips of stems, along them, out of old wood, or from the base of the plant

Terminal

Each stem finishes by becoming the inflorescence - the usual case, and what a foxglove, a yarrow or an allium does

Axillary

Inflorescences arise at nodes along the stems, each on its own short stalk, while the stems go on being stems and bear no flowers themselves. Wisteria, laburnum, birch and hazel. The stalks are not branches: they carry no leaves and sit outside Branch Density and Branching Zone, so those keep describing the plant's woody shape. Pair with Orientation to make them hang

Internodal

From partway along an internode rather than at a node. Uncommon, but real - and the position along the internode is settable below

Leaf-opposed

At a node, but on the far side of the stem from the leaf rather than in its axil - oppositifolious, as grapes and pepper are. Half a turn round from where an axillary one would sit; everything else about it matches Axillary

Cauliflorous

Straight out of wood laid down seasons earlier on the TRUNK, well below the leaves - cauliflory, as figs and cacao do. Defined by age rather than position: nothing appears until a node has carried for the stated number of steps, so a young plant shows none

Ramiflorous

The same old-wood break as Cauliflorous, but along the BRANCHES instead of the trunk - ramiflory, as redbud does on bare limbs. Shares the Wood Age gate; the two differ only in which stems may bear it

Basal

From the root crown, straight out of the ground rather than from anywhere up a stem - violets, many bulbs, and a primrose's scapes. Arises at once rather than waiting on Wood Age: a basal scape is the first thing such a plant does

Adventitious

From old wood that never carried a meristem at all - scattered between the nodes, following no phyllotaxis. The one position whose buds are made rather than found, which is what makes it adventitious. Shares the Wood Age gate; use Per Node to set how many break from each internode

Per Nodewhole numbermappable
default 1 · 1 to 6 on the slider (1 to ∞ typed) · shown for Flower

How many inflorescences arise at each position the attachment picks - 1 is a single one, higher fans a cluster out from the same point. This is what a 'terminal cluster' or an 'axillary cluster' is: a count applied to a position, not a position of its own. As one control it clusters any attachment, including ones a fixed pair of cluster entries could never have covered

Orientationchoice
default Parent-aligned · shown for Flower

Which direction this inflorescence prefers to point

Parent-aligned

Prefer to lie along the stem that carries it, whatever that stem is doing. Re-read as the plant grows, so the inflorescence swings when the branch bends. At Strength 0 this is simply the angle it left the stem at, which is what every plant did before orientation existed

Erect

Prefer to point up, against gravity

Horizontal

Prefer to lie level, perpendicular to gravity. Level is a whole plane, so it keeps the compass direction the bud already had - radially out from its own stem - rather than sending every inflorescence to one side of the plant

Pendulous

Prefer to hang, with gravity

Custom

Prefer the angle set below, measured from the parent stem's own direction rather than from world vertical - so it is stated relative to the stem and swings with it

Strengthnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1 · shown for Flower

How far the inflorescence is pulled from the direction it would naturally leave the stem at, toward the preferred direction above. 0 leaves it exactly as it grew; 1 pulls it fully onto the preference. It is a preference rather than a rule - even at 1 the result keeps some of where it came from, and the stem's own weight then bends it further, so an organ is not forced onto exact vertical. It also sets how sharply the turn happens: the turn is always spread over the same short run of nodes, so a bigger pull bends harder over that run. Higher is sharper, and no value gives a hard corner

Reach It As Flowers Opencheckbox
default off · shown for Flower

Arrive at the preferred direction as the inflorescence fills with flowers, rather than over its first few nodes - upright while it is a bud, bowed over once laden. Different from Droop, which bends the finished stem: this moves while the inflorescence is still growing, so it changes where the flowers are actually placed

Flowers
Branching
Depthwhole numbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 12 · shown for Flower

Makes the inflorescence COMPOUND. At each place it would have put a flower it puts a whole inflorescence of its own kind instead, this many times over. 0 is simple. 1 turns a raceme into a panicle, an umbel into a compound umbel (carrot, cow parsley), a corymb into a compound corymb (yarrow, elder) and a spike into a compound spike (wheat). 2 gives the triple umbels real cow parsley makes. On a cyme it is instead how many times the tip relays, so a long zigzag chain wants 8 or more. Independent of the Branching levels, which stay the plant's own vegetative branching - a plant can have several levels of branch under two of inflorescence, and one number cannot say both. Watch the count: every level multiplies it by Rays (or by Relays per Node on a cyme), and it multiplies again by however many branch tips the plant itself has. Depth 2 on a bushy plant is thousands of flowers

Countwhole numbermappable
default 7 · 1 to 200 · shown for Flower

How many branches the main stem of the inflorescence carries. Separate from Flower Count, which is how many flowers each of those branches ends up with - one number used to serve both, so ten branches of three flowers was not expressible. Only used by Panicle

Anglenumbermappable
default 45 · -90 to 90 · shown for Flower

Which way an inflorescence branch leaves the main stem, measured from perpendicular: 0 is straight out sideways, +90 flat up along the stem, -90 flat down. Separate from the plant's own Branch Angle, which describes its woody branches. This is the main thing separating a diffuse, open panicle from a contracted, spike-like one. On a cyme this is the zigzag: it is the angle each relay leaves the spent tip above it at, so +90 carries straight on with no visible kink and lower values fork harder every generation. The kink is exactly 90 minus this

Spacingnumbermappable
default 1.5 · 0 to 4 on the slider (0 to 8 typed) · shown for Flower

Gap between successive branches along the main stem of the inflorescence, relative to an ordinary internode. Separate from Flower Spacing on purpose: a panicle stands its branches well apart while crowding the flowers on them, and one number cannot say both. Only used by Panicle

Nodeswhole numbermappable
default 2 · 1 to 20 · shown for Flower

Nodes an inflorescence branch lays down before it starts flowering - the bare basal stretch of a panicle branch. Only used by Panicle

Lengthnumbermappable
default 1 · 0 to 4 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for Flower

How far apart the nodes of an inflorescence branch sit, and so how long the branch is. Separate from Branch Nodes, which is how many flowers it carries - before this a branch could only be lengthened by making it carry more. Only used by Panicle

Widthnumbermappable
default 0.6 · 0.01 to 1 · shown for Flower

A branch's thickness where it leaves the main stem, as a fraction of that stem's own thickness there - so 1.0 is exactly as thick as the stem it comes off, and it cannot go above that. Same as Pedicel Width. Its graph is the taper along one branch, base to tip, and shapes only the taper - the base width is this number's to set. Thinner branches also arch further, because bending resists as the fourth power of radius. Only used by Panicle

Bendnumbermappable
default 0 · -1 to 1 · shown for Flower

A steady arch along each inflorescence branch, held in the branch's own plane - so it turns with the branch rather than always heading for the ground. 1 is a quarter turn from base to tip. This is shape; Branch Droop below is weight. Only used by Panicle

Droopnumbermappable
default 0 · -1 to 1 · shown for Flower

How far an inflorescence branch turns out of the way it was aimed, over its whole length. Negative sags it toward the ground, -1 hanging straight down; positive lifts it toward vertical - the same sign as Angle and Bend above it, and what an erect panicle's upswept primaries need. Distinct from Peduncle Droop, which only bends the stretch below the lowest flower and therefore cannot touch a branch that carries branches rather than flowers. Unlike Bend it is measured against gravity, so it does not turn with the branch

Countwhole numbermappable
default 7 · 1 to 200 · shown for Flower

Flowers per inflorescence. Ignored by Solitary and by the cymose kinds, which get their count from how many times they relay instead - that is Branching Depth times Relays per Node

Per Whorlwhole numbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 16 · shown for Flower

How many flowers each node of the inflorescence carries, in a ring around the stem. 0 follows the plant's own leaf arrangement, which is one flower per leaf position - so 0 is exactly what every kind did before this existed. Separate from Trunk Pattern on purpose: one flower is placed per leaf position, so asking for a six-flowered whorl through the phyllotaxis also gives the leafy stem below six leaves per node. A mint has two. This is the flowering region stating its own arrangement

Spiralnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 360 · shown for Flower

The flowers' own spiral up the inflorescence: each flowering node's flower turned this many degrees round the stem from the last (137.5 is the golden angle). 0 follows the plant's leaf arrangement. Lets a spike spiral while its leaves stay two-ranked, as a grass's do. Flowers per Whorl (2 or more) replaces it

Spacingnumbermappable
default 0.5 · 0.02 to 2 · shown for Flower

Spacing between flowers along the axis, relative to the leafy stem's own internode length. Below 1 packs the flowering region tighter than the stem below it, which is how most inflorescences sit

Spacing Basenumbermappable
default 0.045 m · 0.001 m to ∞ · shown for Flower

The inflorescence's spacing base: the distance between flowers is this times Flower Spacing (Branch Spacing on a branched rachis), the same on every stem and branch. Stem and branch internodes are the Branching levels' Length instead

Weightnumbermappable
default 0.0004 · 0 to 0.01 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed) · shown for Flower

How heavy a full-size flower or head is. This is now the main thing that nods a blooming tip: a heavy head on a thin stem hangs, a light one stands up. Flower mass grows with the CUBE of Flower Size, so doubling a head's size makes it eight times heavier - size and weight together decide the droop

Young Sizenumbermappable
default 0.2 · 0 to 1 · shown for Flower

How big an inflorescence is the moment it is laid down, as a share of mature - its flower spacing, flower size and pedicel length and width all start here and grow to full as it develops. Only the youngest racemes (started near the end of the season) show it; a mature one is always full size. The curve beside it shapes the growth from this start to full

Spreadnumbermappable
default 360 · 0 to 360 · shown for Flower

How much of the stem's circumference the flowers occupy. 360 is the full circle the leaf arrangement already gives; narrow it to crowd them onto one side, the way a foxglove does, and 0 puts every flower on a single line

Heliotropismnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1 · shown for Flower

How far each flower turns its face toward the Sun Object, after growth. The nodding-sunflower case: the stem stays where gravity left it, the head turns up to the sun and its own stalk curves with it (a stalk a branch leaves stays straight); 0 is off

Pedicel
Widthnumbermappable
default 0.3 · 0.01 to 1 · shown for Flower

How thick each pedicel is where it leaves the stem, as a fraction of the stem's own thickness there. 1 continues the stem's width, which reads as a short branch; most plants carry conspicuously finer pedicels than that

Bendnumbermappable
default 0.7 · 0 to 1 · shown for Flower

How strongly each pedicel curves. 0 gives straight spokes; higher makes it leave the stem sideways and turn up harder on its way to the flower, the way a real corymb does. A pedicel never swings wider than its own flower. This is shape only and does NOT move the flower - the pedicel arcs between the same two endpoints, so Length and Angle still decide where the flower sits

Lengthnumbermappable
default 0.03 m · 0 m to ∞ · shown for Flower

Length of the pedicel - the little stalk between the stem and each flower. A corymb lengthens the lower ones automatically; a spike and a catkin ignore this, because their flowers are sessile and have no pedicel at all

Anglenumbermappable
default 30 · -90 to 90 · shown for Flower

How far a pedicel tilts off horizontal. 0 leaves the stem straight out sideways, positive swings it up toward the tip, negative hangs it down for a drooping raceme. Plus or minus 90 presses it flat against the stem

Bloom
Orderchoice
default Bottom first · shown for Flower

Which flowers open first. Later ones are still opening, so they read smaller and tighter

Bottom first

Lowest flowers open first and are furthest along

Top first

Highest flowers open first

Outside first

Outer flowers open first, working inward

Middle first

Central flowers open first, working outward

Timing
Smooth bloom stage blendingcheckbox
default off · shown for Flower

Blend smoothly between neighbouring bloom stages instead of snapping from one to the next. Every stage must have identical topology - stages baked from one flower do; a set of separately modelled flowers will not, and will scramble

Bloomchoice
default From Age · shown for Flower

Where each flower's openness comes from

From Age

Flowers open as the plant matures: Progress is worked out from Age and the point in its life this species starts flowering. Scrub Age and the plant grows and blooms together

Manual

Progress is the slider below, independent of Age. This is the one to keyframe when the bloom needs its own timing

Static

No timeline at all: each flower shows the stage its own bloom order calls for, so the first to open is out and the last is a bud

Spreadnumbermappable
default 0.5 · 0 to 1 · shown for Flower

How staggered the opening is. 0 opens every flower in lockstep; 1 means the last flower in the bloom order does not begin until Progress reaches 1, so the opening travels up the inflorescence as a wave. Under From Age the stagger already comes from when each flower was actually born, so this reads instead as how quickly a flower opens once it appears - higher leaves fewer buds at the tip

Masks
Listlist

One row per filter on a component: a colour swatch, the attribute it reads, an invert marker, a per-attribute preview eye, and a mute. The window is tuned in the details below -- the row stays a legible summary. data is the component PG (only the active component's filters are drawn), reaching the growth PG through the object it lives on.

Attributechoice
default Height · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit
Height

How far up the plant the organ sits (0 base, 1 top)

Branch Depth

How many levels of branching from the main stem -- 0 on the main stem, rising with each branch order (normalised to the plant's deepest branch)

Branch Index

A distinct value per branch, so you can pick out particular branches (normalised across the plant's branches)

On Branch

0 on the main stem, 1 on any branch -- the simple stem-vs-branch split

Node Index

Which node up its own axis the organ sits at, 0 at the base to 1 at the tip

Factor

Position along the organ's own axis, 0 at the axis base to 1 at its tip

Age

When the organ was made, 0 with the plant's first growth to 1 at the last -- low is old, high is new

Split Depth

How deep inside a fork / inflorescence the organ sits, 0 on vegetative stem rising with each split

Shade

How shaded the organ is by the plant's own canopy, 0 in open sky to 1 fully shaded -- sampled from the self-shading light field, so a dense clump reads its shaded interior

Bloom

A flower's place on the bloom order (flowers only)

Random

Seeded per-organ noise, for scattered thinning

Apex

1 on a shoot's own tip bud (its apex), 0 on axillary buds and every other organ -- keep only tip buds, or invert to keep only side buds

Custom Attribute

One of this plant's own attributes (Mapping & Classification panel): a distance to an object, noise, or two channels combined

Class

One of this plant's named classes (Mapping & Classification panel): 1 where that class's own mask stack keeps the point, 0 elsewhere -- build a class once, reuse and chain it

On Inflorescence

1 on an inflorescence -- the flowering nodes past an axis's leafy part, and the branches and stalks the inflorescence releases -- 0 on the leafy stem. Invert to keep only the vegetative part

Minnumber
default 0 · 0 to 1 · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

Low edge of the keep band. Points below Min are dropped

Maxnumber
default 1 · 0 to 1 · shown for Leaf, Bract, Bud, Fruit

High edge of the keep band. Points above Max are dropped -- so Min 0.4, Max 0.5 keeps only the 0.4-0.5 slice

Physiology

panel

How the whole plant behaves: its tropisms and timing, stiffness, pruning, surface, its response to light, obstacles and effectors, senescence, and its rig and wind.

Tropismsfold

Gravitropismnumbermappable
default 0.35 · 0 to 1

How strongly a stem corrects back toward the angle it is trying to hold. Higher makes stems stiff and true; lower lets them wander

Autotropismnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1

How much older stem straightens back to true as it ages, so the wander stays a live nodding tip on a tidy stem instead of a wobble all the way down. Higher keeps a shorter, tidier live zone at the very tip. 0 is off

Circumnutationnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 15 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

How far the growing tip nods off-axis each step in a coiling, helical sweep -- the spiralling seen in growth timelapses. Unlike Irregularity, which wanders at random, this winds a coherent helix. Its size is fought by Gravitropism, so raise Autotropism to see it on an upright plant. 0 is off

Circumnutation Ratenumbermappable
default 137.5 · -360 to 360

How far the nod turns around the stem each step -- the pitch of the helix, its sign the handedness (left- vs right-winding). Does nothing while Circumnutation is 0

Timingfold

Internode Elongationchoicecurve
default Sequential

How each internode stretches to its full length after it forms. Picking one sets the Internode Elongation curve and Duration; edit either and it reads Custom

Sequential

Each internode reaches its full length before the next one forms -- one stretching at a time

Overlapping

Several internodes stretch at once: the lower ones keep growing for a while after new ones form above (most herbs)

Delayed

A new internode stays short while the next nodes form, then stretches -- compressed young growth that spreads out later

Custom

Your own curve and Duration

Durationwhole numbermappable
default 5 · 1 to 20 on the slider (1 to ∞ typed)

Growth steps an internode takes to reach its full length after it forms (one node forms per step): 1 = done before the next forms, higher = several stretching at once

Leaf Expansionwhole numbermappablecurve
default 7 · 1 to 30 on the slider (1 to ∞ typed)

Growth steps a leaf takes to grow from a tiny primordium to its full size, along the Leaf Expansion curve -- longer keeps young leaves small for longer

Stem Thickening

Stiffnessfold

Presetchoicemappable
default Custom

A named starting point for the physical controls below. Picking one stamps its stiffness, variance, leaf and flower weight and stiffness curve, then snaps back to Custom - so the dropdown never claims a preset you have since edited

Custom

Your own values, below

Herbaceous - Upright

A normal upright perennial stem

Herbaceous - Lax

Soft, lax stem with a gently softening tip

Herbaceous - Climbing

Very flexible, a vine or scrambler

Grass Culm

Stiff, light, upright

Reed

Stiffer than a grass culm

Succulent

Soft tissue but heavy - a fleshy stem

Woody - Sapling

Young wood, stiff but still bends

Woody - Shrub

A firm woody shrub

Woody - Rigid

Near-hardwood, barely bends

Weeping

Rigid base, soft tip - the lamppost / weeping habit

Pruningfoldclosed by default

Prune Limbsbutton

Draw a labelled glyph for every node, bud, apex, leaf and flower, and read one by pointing at it. P pins a card, X prunes the limb. Click again to turn off

Keep Dead Woodcheckbox
default off

Whether a pruned limb stays as grey dead wood, or is removed entirely (the default). Distinct from the Age/Shade default, which keeps dead wood standing -- pruning is a gardener's cut, so it removes by default

Clear Pruningbutton

Restore every pruned limb on this plant

Surfacefold

Smoothnesswhole numbermappable
default 4 · 1 to 8 on the slider (1 to 16 typed)

How densely rings are placed along the stems. The stem is a smooth curve through every node; at 4 its faces are close to square, so bends read round and the welded junctions shade cleanly. Higher costs geometry

Weld Junctionscheckbox
default on

Merge every stem and branch into one watertight mesh, joined at the junctions, instead of separate tubes overlapping each other

Weld Rangenumbermappable
default 0.5 · 0 to 2 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

How round each weld is: the radius of the fillet that blends a branch into its parent, in branch radii (smaller in a shallow crotch). Small keeps the join tight; large blends it out over more of the stem. 0 leaves a hard crease

Light Stalkscheckbox
default off

Build pedicels with four sides, and give stems too thin to show bark fewer rings on their straight runs. For a plant with thousands of flowers. Branch welds and bends keep their density

Weldbutton

Weld the active plant's stems: every junction joined and filleted into one mesh, with UVs. Builds in the background -- keep working meanwhile. Changing parameters after welding will require rebuilding the welds

Lightfoldclosed by default

Light Seekingnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1

How far growing tips turn toward the light each step. Applied after Gravitropism, so a shaded shoot leans out from under whatever is shading it even though gravity would hold it upright. 0 ignores light direction

Leaf Heliotropismnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1

How far each leaf turns its blade to face the sun, after growth. Set Sun Object below to the thing to track. Unlike an Align Up effector this aims each blade at the sun rather than rotating the whole leaf set; 0 is off

Sun Objectpicker

The object leaves turn to face, for Leaf Heliotropism (each flower component picks its own). They aim at wherever it sits relative to the plant, so move it to place the sun -- any object works (an empty, a lamp, a mesh). Empty means no heliotropism

Obstaclesfoldclosed by default

Collectionpicker

Objects this plant grows around. Any mesh will do, and closed shapes work best. They block growth and cast shade. Empty means nothing is in the way

Clearancenumbermappable
default 0 m · 0 m to 0.5 m on the slider (0 m to ∞ typed)

How far from a surface this plant keeps its growing tips. Tips curve away as they approach, and one that runs out of room stops there instead of growing through. 0 turns obstacle response off entirely

Groundfoldclosed by default

Objectpicker

A terrain mesh the plant rests on: a stem that bends down to it lies along its surface instead of the flat ground at the plant's base. Only the bend reads it -- growth is not steered. Empty means flat ground

Effectorsfoldclosed by default

Collectionpicker

Effector empties that steer this plant by hand - attract, repel, forbid or aim. Unlike Light and Obstacles there is nothing to enable first: an effector in this collection acts straight away. Empty means nothing steers it

Add Effectorbutton

Add an effector at the 3D cursor that steers the active plant's growth, and link it to that plant

Senescencefoldclosed by default

Age Senescence
Shade Deathnumbermappable
default 0 · 0 to 1

After growth, each branch is judged by the light at its base; below this it dies and takes its subtree with it. 0 (default) never kills. The plant shades itself, so this works with no obstacle in the scene; add obstacles overhead to shade a lower crown. 1.0 kills anything out of full sky

Keep Dead Woodcheckbox
default on

Whether a dead branch stays as grey dead wood, or is removed entirely. Its leaves and flowers are shed either way -- a dead branch is bare

Dead Colournumber
default 0.35, 0.28, 0.2, 1 · 0 to 1

What dead tissue is tinted toward. A shader sampling the Color vertex attribute shows it in a render; the Senescence debug view shows it in the viewport regardless of material

Rigfoldclosed by default

Bone Angle
StemsnumberDebug Tools
default 15° · 0° to 60°

How far this level's stems or branches may bend along one bone before the rig starts the next: straight runs share a bone, bends get more. 0 = a bone per node. Read when the rig is built

Branches 1number
default 15° · 0° to 60°

How far this level's stems or branches may bend along one bone before the rig starts the next: straight runs share a bone, bends get more. 0 = a bone per node. Read when the rig is built

Build Rigbutton

Build a skeletal rig for the plant as it stands: a bone chain down every stem and branch (straight runs share a bone -- each level's Bone Angle), a bone per leaf, bract, flower, bud and fruit, and the welded mesh skinned to it with smooth weights. The plant then shows the rig (Rig View). Rebuilding replaces the previous rig

Rig Viewcheckbox
default off

Show this plant as its baked rig -- the skinned mesh, posed and animated by the bones -- instead of the live build. Still the one object you select and edit; any edit that regrows drops back to the live plant and marks the rig out of date

Show Bonescheckbox
default off

Draw the rig's bones over the plant in Rig View

Displaychoice
default Octahedral

How the rig's bones are drawn in the viewport. Display only -- the skeleton and an export are the same either way

Octahedral

Bones as octahedra (Blender's default)

Stick

Bones as thin lines -- the least clutter on a dense rig

B-Bone

Bones as boxes

Envelope

Bones as their deform envelopes

Wire

Bones as wireframe lines

Fast Previewcheckbox
default on

Play the rig fast in Rig View: only the stems deform, and every leaf and flower stays a GPU instance that follows its bone -- the same look, a fraction of the work per frame. Off: the full skinned mesh deforms (slow with many flowers). Falls back to the full mesh while Vertex Wind is on. The export always writes the full mesh

Export Rigbutton

Export the rig as a skeletal mesh -- the bones and the skinned mesh in their bind pose, with weights, UVs, materials and the vertex colours -- to FBX or USD (by the file's extension), the plant's root at the origin; and beside it <name>_wind.json, the simulation groups Unreal's Dynamic Wind imports (Import Dynamic Wind Data). Build Rig first

Export Nanite Assemblybutton

Export the rig as a skeletal-mesh Nanite Assembly (USD) for Unreal 5.7+ Nanite Foliage: the stems as a skinned base mesh, every leaf and flower that is one of its component's meshes as an instance of it, bound to its own bone; flowers on their bloom stage. Beside it <name>_wind.json for Dynamic Wind. Build Rig first

Windfoldclosed by default

Bone Windcheckbox
default off

An approximation of Unreal's wind, to preview in Blender: the rig's bones sway with the gusts, thin limp parts most, everything on them riding along. Nothing of it is exported -- Unreal simulates the real sway itself, from the wind groups Export Rig writes (made from the same stem flexibility this preview uses). Plays on the timeline in Rig View; needs a rig (Build Rig)

Strengthnumber
default 1 · 0 to 4 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

How hard the preview wind pushes the bones. Preview only -- Unreal's wind strength comes from its own wind source in the level

Stiffnessnumber
default 1 · 0.01 to 8 on the slider (0.01 to ∞ typed)

Trims how far the preview bends -- higher sways less. Each bone's own give still comes from the stem's flexibility, so thin limp parts sway while thick ones barely move. Preview only -- it does not change what Unreal gets

Vertex Windcheckbox
default off

Flutter leaves and petals with a wave driven by the vertex colours (Red: still at the base, free at the tip; Green / Blue: each leaf and plant out of step). A viewport preview of what an engine's foliage material does at runtime from the same colours -- never exported or baked. Needs a rig (Build Rig)

Strengthnumber
default 1 · 0 to 4 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

How far leaf and petal tips flutter. Shares Direction, Gust Speed and Turbulence with Bone Wind

Gusts
Directionnumber
default 120 · 0 to 360

Preview wind heading in degrees (0-360) on the ground plane; gusts swirl around it. Preview only -- Unreal takes its wind direction from the level

Gust Scalenumber
default 2.5 · 0.001 to 4 on the slider (0.001 to ∞ typed)

Gust spatial frequency -- higher gives smaller, tighter gusts

Gust Speednumber
default 1 · 0 to 3 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

How fast the gust field drifts and evolves over time

Turbulencenumber
default 1.5 · 0 to 2 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

Swirl amount -- curl-noise eddying added to the wind heading

Wind Seedwhole number
default 0 · 0 to 2147483647 on the slider (0 to ∞ typed)

Randomizes the whole gust pattern -- each value is a wholly different field (and decorrelates this plant from others)

Show GustschoiceDebug Tools
default Off

Visualise the wind noise field -- blue = lull, green = neutral, red = gust

Off

No wind debug view

Plane

A 2D plane coloured by the animated gust field

Volume

A 3D voxel grid coloured by the gust field

Both

Both the plane and the volume

Curve shapes

named shapes for every curve field

A field of type 'curve' is a small graph over a normalised x (its x_axis says what x means, e.g. base->tip or seedling->mature). Set it to one of the named shapes below as {"shape": "<key>"}; every curve field accepts every shape. Raw {"points": [[x, y], ...]} is a rare escape hatch for a shape none of the names fit.

max
Max
min
Min
half
Half
rise
Rise
droop
Droop
linear_growth
Linear Growth
linear_decay
Linear Decay
exp_growth
Exponential Growth
exp_decay
Exponential Decay
round
Round
s_curve
S-Curve
fade_in
Fade In
fade_out
Fade Out
rosette
Rosette
dome
Dome

Glossary

botanical terms used here
Acropetal
Developing or opening from the base upward.
Adventitious
Arising in an unusual place, from tissue that carried no bud.
Apex
The growing tip of a stem or axis.
Axil
The angle between a leaf and the stem above it.
Axillary
Arising in a leaf axil.
Basipetal
Developing or opening from the tip downward.
Bolting
The rapid elongation of a stem into flower, especially from a rosette.
Bract
A reduced or modified leaf, often at the base of a flower or inflorescence.
Cauliflorous
Flowering directly from the trunk or main stem, as cacao does.
Corymb
A flat-topped inflorescence whose lower flowers have longer stalks.
Cyme
An inflorescence whose axis ends in a flower, further flowers arising below it.
Decussate
Leaves in opposite pairs, each pair at right angles to the next.
Determinate
An axis that ends in a flower and stops growing.
Dichotomous
Branching by the growing tip forking into two equal branches.
Distichous
Leaves in two opposite ranks, all in one plane.
Indeterminate
An axis that keeps growing, flowering along its length.
Inflorescence
The flower-bearing part of a plant, and the arrangement of its flowers.
Internode
The length of stem between two nodes.
Lignified
Hardened with woody tissue.
Meristem
A region of dividing cells from which new growth arises.
Monopodial
Growth from a single persistent main axis.
Node
A point on a stem where leaves, buds or branches arise.
Panicle
A branched inflorescence, a raceme of racemes.
Pedicel
The stalk of a single flower.
Peduncle
The stalk of an inflorescence, or of a solitary flower.
Pendulous
Hanging downward.
Phyllotaxis
The arrangement of leaves around a stem.
Pseudomonopodial
A false single axis, built from a series of dominant forks.
Raceme
An unbranched inflorescence of stalked flowers along a continuing axis.
Rachis
The main axis of an inflorescence or a compound leaf.
Ramiflorous
Flowering from old wood along the branches rather than the trunk.
Rosette
A circular cluster of leaves at the base of a plant.
Scape
A leafless flowering stalk rising from the ground.
Secund
With flowers or leaves all turned to one side.
Sessile
Without a stalk, attached directly.
Spike
An unbranched inflorescence of sessile flowers.
Sympodial
Growth continued by successive lateral branches, the tip stopping each time.
Terminal
At the tip of a stem or axis.
Tiller
A shoot arising from the base of a grass or similar plant.
Umbel
An inflorescence whose flower stalks all arise from one point.
Vegetativeness
How strongly a meristem keeps making stem rather than flowers.
Whorl
Three or more leaves or flowers arising at one node.
